observations: body (table): the table is boxed by double rules, the head separated from the rows by a thin rule; the heads are in small capitals with the explanations in small roman. The degrees, parts, minutes and seconds stand in columns aligned on the right; the names of the planets are bold.

body (table): the sines to the radius 60 are right for the Moon (5p 14′ 48″, rounded 5p 15′), Saturn (6p 29′ 50″), Jupiter (11p 30′), Venus (43p 8′ 54″, rounded 43p 9′) and Mercury (22p 30′ 31″); for Mars 60 sin 41° 9′ is 39p 28′ 55″, and the 39p 27′ 22″ of the table is the sine of 41° 7′. Ptolemy's radii give back the greatest equations 6° 13′, 11° 3′, 41° 10′, 46° 0′ and 22° 1′.
body L9: the Arabic letters are the abjad numerals كه = 25 and كز = 27.
body L8, L11-L13, L20-L21, L25-L26, L31: the dashes of the transliterated names and of «234–236», «630–632» are long dashes (5.4 to 5.5 pt).
notes_left L1: the dash of «al–Farghānī» measures 4.2 pt, a long dash.

body L9, L16, L22-L23: the dashes before «In», after «a)» and «b)» measure 9.8 to 10.0 pt and are transcribed as dashes; that after «Temporis aequatio.» measures 7.2 pt; those of «33-37» and «8-13» in the heads are hyphens (3.5 pt).
body L23: a heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition, which continues on p. 222.
body L31: the title of Delambre's book is printed in bold italic.
source_authority: Controlling master page image. Embedded text is not the authority for a reading.
transcription_convention: Source line breaks, hyphenation, quotation signs and word-level type distinctions retained. L numbers count text-bearing lines.
review_responsibility: Transcribed by Claude from the page images; Greek, Arabic, numbers and signs read on enlarged images. Not reviewed by a person.
